{{Short description|Equations involving the trace of a matrix}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''trace identity''' is any [[equation]] involving the [[Trace (linear algebra)|trace]] of a [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]].

==Properties==

Trace identities are invariant under simultaneous [[Conjugation (group theory)|conjugation]].

==Uses==

They are frequently used in the [[invariant theory]] of <math>n \times n</math> matrices to find the [[Generating set|generators]] and [[Relation (mathematics)|relations]] of the [[Invariant theory|ring of invariants]], and therefore are useful in answering questions similar to that posed by [[Hilbert's fourteenth problem]].

==Examples==

* The [[Cayley–Hamilton theorem]] says that every square matrix satisfies its own [[characteristic polynomial]]. This also implies that all square matrices satisfy <math display="block">\operatorname{tr}\left(A^n\right) - c_{n-1} \operatorname{tr}\left(A^{n - 1}\right) + \cdots + (-1)^n n \det(A) = 0\,</math> where the coefficients <math>c_i</math> are given by the [[elementary symmetric polynomial]]s of the [[eigenvalue]]s of {{mvar|A}}.
* All [[square matrices]] satisfy <math display=block>\operatorname{tr}(A) = \operatorname{tr}\left(A^\mathsf{T}\right).\,</math>
